speaker: Chairman Charlotte Lane
role: Chairman, Public Service Commission of West Virginia
text: Good morning. I'm Charlotte Lane, chairman of the Public Service Commission of West Virginia. With me are Commissioners Renee Larrick and Bill Raney. Please check your cell phones to make sure they're turned off or set to vibrate only. And if you need to take a call during this proceeding, please step outside. We are here today to conduct an evidentiary hearing in case number 26-000075. NextEra Energy Transmission MidAtlantic, Inc. On January 30, 2026, NextEra Energy Transmission MidAtlantic filed an application seeking a certificate of public convenience and necessity pursuant to West Virginia Code 24-2-11A. The application requests commission authorization to construct, finance, own, and operate the West Virginia portions of the Mid-Atlantic Resiliency Link Project, otherwise known as MARL project. A proposed 107.5 mile 500 kV interstate electric transmission line. and the West Virginia components of the MARL project consist of 58.9 miles of transmission line and related facilities related are located in Monongalia County, Preston, Mineral and Hampshire counties. Only the West Virginia portion of the MARL project are before us today. The purpose of this hearing is to develop a complete evidentiary record regarding the proposed MARL project. Before we begin taking testimony, the commission would like to address several procedural matters and remind the parties of the requirements governing this hearing. Given the large number of parties participating this proceeding, these procedures are necessary to ensure that the hearing produ proceeds fairly, efficiently, and in an orderly manner. First, the commission recognizes that parties have raised questions and concerns regarding the conduct of this hearing. This is an evidentary hearing, not a public comment hearing. Only parties who have filed pre-filed testimony may testify at this hearing except upon leave of the commission for good cause shown. The commission will not permit opening statements by any parties. The parties positions are reflected in their filings and pre-filed testimony and the hearing will proceed directly to the presentation of evidence. Second, the commission reminds all parties that testimony and questioning must be relevant to the issues the commission is required to consider. Accordingly, the commission expects parties to focus their testimony and questioning on the requirements set forth in West Virginia Code 24-2-11A. The statute states, "No public utility, person or cooperation may begin construction of a high voltage transmission line of 200,000 volts or over. Which line is not an ordinary extension of an existing system in the usual course of business as defined by the public service commission unless and until it or he or she has obtained from the public service commission a certificate of public convenience and necessity approving the construction and proposed location of the transmission line within 60 days after the filing of the application or if hearing is held on the application. ation within 90 days after final submission or oral argument or brief. The commission may approve the application if it finds that the proposed transmission line will economically, adequately, and reliably contribute to meeting the present and anticipated requirements for electric power of the customers served by the applicant or is necessary and desirable for present and anticipated reliability of service for electric generation for its service area or region. will be in the best interests of West Virginia customers and its citizens and will result in an acceptable balance between reasonable power needs and reasonable environmental factors. The commission may impose conditions upon the approval of the application or modify the applicant's approval to achieve an acceptable balance between reasonable power needs and reasonable environmental factors. Testimony and cross-examination must be directed to these statutory conditions or considerations and the issues properly before the commission. The commission will not permit irrelevant, repetitive, or dup duplicative testimony or questioning. If another party has already adequately addressed a matter with a witness, there is no need to ask the same questions again. Third, the commission previously required each party to identify the intervenor witnesses that the party anticipated cross-examining. The commission will not impose a predetermined time limit or numerical limit on the questions that an intervenor may ask a witness. However, all questions must be relevant to the issues in this proceeding directed to the testimony of the witness being questioned and not duplicative of questions already asked. Cross-examination is not an opportunity to testify, make an argument, or conduct discovery. The the commission expects parties with similar interest to coordinate their questioning and avoid unnecessary repetition. Under procedural rule 12.6.5 when interveners have substantially center similar interests and positions. The commission may limit the number of parties who may cross-examine witnesses, make and argue motions, or object on behalf of those interveners to expedite the hearing. The commission also reserves the authority to impose reasonable limitations on questioning when necessary to main and to maintain an orderly and efficient hearing. Fourth, all witnesses scheduled for a particular day must be present at the beginning of that day and prepared to testify when called. The hearing will generally begin at 9:30 and break for lunch between 12:30 and 1:30. The commission does not intend to establish a fixed ending time for each day. Instead, the commission will continue each day until the scheduled hearings have completed their testimony and all appropriate questioning has concluded. The commission will determine when recesses or adjournments are necessary. Fifth, if a party wishes to object, please state that you have an objection and wait to be recognized. Once recognized, briefly state the basis for the objection. The commission may allow a response from another party before ruling on the objection. Six, the commission reminds corporations, limited liability companies, homeowners associations, nonprofit organization, county commissions, and other artificial legal entities that they must be represented in this proceeding by an attorney licensed to practice law in West Virginia. An officer, employee, member, or other representative who is not at an attorney may not act as legal counsel or represent such an entity during this hearing. The commission recognizes that many parties in this proceeding are participating without part counsel. All parties, whether represented by counsel or appearing pro se, are expected to comply with the commission's procedural orders, the orders previously entered in this case, and the directions of the commission during this hearing. Finally, the commission has received recent motions requesting that it impose certain conditions if it approves the proposed project. The motions raise issue about potential construction related impacts and appropriate measures to address them. The commission will defer rolling on the requested conditions until it is considered the evidentiary record. The parties may address these matters through relevant testimony and cross-examination during the hearing. The commission will determine whether any conditions are warranted when asking its final when making its final determination on the application. Ordinarily, at the beginning of a hearing, the commission calls upon each party to enter an appearance on the record. Given the number of parties participating in this proceeding, the commission will instead use a daily attendance sheet to identify the parties present at the hearing. All parties attending the hearing shall sign the attendance sheet each day they are present. If you are present today and have not signed the attendance sheet, please do so now. The attendance sheet is intended solely to assist the commission in managing the hearing and maintaining a record of attendance. Signing or failing to sign the attendance sheet does not affect a party's status or any rights otherwise afforded to that party in this proceeding. The commission will now take appearances on the record from those parties represented by counsel.

Uh when you have an interstate like that and the traffic continues to grow on it, it leads to congestion that casts this impact on not only the inter regional or the state or or interstate needs in terms of moving merchandise or moving people or ease of commute or saving fuel. But it also poses lots of inconvenience to folks who live in the intermediate offramps and on-ramps that utilize that highway. Now when when the federal government or the state government initiates a project to build another highway to parallel and offload the existing highway with the offramps and you do not introduce new offramps, the result is going to be that the flow on the original highway is going to go down and people will start to experience less congestion, less safety issues, shorter commute times, more efficiencies. I think that is very close to what's being proposed here by introducing MARL through West Virginia without necessarily having substations inside West Virginia. These impacts are there. They will have economic impacts that are felt today by the people of West Virginia and across the interconnection in PJM. text: Okay, before we take our first intervenor because of the confusion about public utility property taxes, I am submitting a memo as a commission exhibit number one. And Ryan, do you want to pass this out, please, to all of the parties? Oh, and give one to the court reporter, please. And I'm going to read into the record the relevant information. It occurred to me that the testimony that we have had so far was all over the board about what taxes utility property pays. And I I just want to clear the record. So statewide assessment in West Virginia public utility property is assessed by the the state under West Virginia code chapter 11-6. The board of public works determines the assessed value of public utility property. The state tax commissioner as chief executive of the state tax division administers the preparation of tenative assessments for consideration and final determination by the board of public works including reviewing company information returns and preparing valuation recommendations. The state auditor allocates the assessment values among the counties and calculates the county taxes assess or based on the assessment rates in each county. The valuation is based on a combination of property net book cost and a calculated value of property based on net operating income. And I've got some examples, but I'm not going to read that into the record. It'll speak for itself. After the board of public works determines the total assessed value, the state auditor aortions the assessed value among the counties in which the utility operates. The allocation can be based on direct assignment of taxable income to a county or an allocation formula. The taxable value of large high-cost facilities that may be located in a single county but which serve the entire utility system are not allocated to only the county containing the facility. The state auditor determines the taxes for each county using applicable levy rates of each county applied to the assessed valuation allocated to each county. Within a limited time period, a utility may appeal a valuation or petition for relief from an erroneous assessment pursuant to West Virginia code. A company operating large electric transmission facilities in West Virginia but having no other utility operations in the state are evaluated the same as public utilities that have production transmission and distribution operate operations in West Virginia. The lack of local generation or distribution operations or lack of local revenue and income does not mean that the transmission facilities must be valued solely by netbook cost. Under the unit method, if applicable, the state may consider the value of the integrated transmission business as a whole and determine a portion of net operating income attributable to West Virginia and then apply the capitalization rate to that net operating income. And with that, I'm going to move that be in the record. And hopefully that will clear up the record as to how utility property is assessed and taxed in West Virginia. Now, let's go to our first intervenor. What?

Those are the inputs that they use in their business when they decide where they want to go. And if those conditions change, as we've seen and as is laid out in my testimony in a couple PJM utilities that I specifically note, uh those data centers will uproots and leave. I mean it it in many cases they do not have significant investments in terms of site control anything like that. They basically come to the local utility and said hey we would like to build this massive facility. So it follows logically that whatever FERC decides might increase the share that large load customers pay for their own interconnections. That is the sort of economic input that makes a data center go you know what I I think I'd like to go further west maybe you know there's this new development in in whatever state. So that's the reason that these two issues are like this because to the extent that cost allocation favors data centers that increases the data center load that we see in sort of this self-fulfilling cycle and if that cycle breaks then we may see significant drops in whether projected data center load or the rate at which projected data center load actually materializes depending on how responsive LSEs are to those changing market conditions and whether the data center companies that no longer intend to build data centers bother to call the LSEs and let them know those plans have been cancelled.
